title: Cut in a window sash rail with a sash brush: paint the putty up to the glass without flooding the pane
instruction: Paint the bare part of the near sash rail to match the painted part, right up to the glass, then lay the brush back on its rest.
context: Cutting in at the glass is the freehand, millimetre-scale part of repainting wooden windows, common home upkeep: the paint must reach the last 1 mm of putty, which seals the glazing, and go no more than 2 mm onto the glass, or the pane is smeared. Here that edge is held along 183 mm with a compliant brush that needs reloading: held about 1 mm too low, the bristles splay onto the glass; about 1 mm too high, they lay nothing.
setup: Four-light pine window sash, 508 x 635 x 28.6 mm (20 x 25 x 1-1/8 in), putty glazed with four 8 x 10 in single-strength lights; bottom rail 85.7 mm, stiles and top rail 60.3 mm, muntins 22.2 mm; cured putty bevels 9.5 mm wide at rails and stiles, 6.35 mm at muntins, glass 3.95 mm below the wood; primed and base-coated grey, lying flat putty side up, fixed on the bench, near rail outer edge 120 mm in front of the arm bases, centred. On each side (mirror images, y = +/-): a Purdy XL Glide 2 in angular trim brush (85 g; 140 x 22 x 15 mm hardwood handle, 25 x 54 x 18 mm ferrule, 68 mm bristles 50.8 mm wide: estimates) lies broad face down across a 165 x 60 x 39.5 mm notched pine rest centred (417.5, +/-350) mm, handle end at x 500 mm, bristles toward the arms, in the air; an open 1-quart paint can (108 mm diameter, 124 mm tall) with 90 mm of dark green water-based enamel stands at (170, +/-360) mm. Layout A: the near rail beside the near-right light is already painted dark green 25 mm wide and the strip beside the near-left light is bare; layout B is the reverse. Nothing else changes. Trials alternate A and B and are averaged; the screenshot shows A. Full coordinates in README.
scoring: Score 0 if at any time: paint lies more than 2 mm onto any glass from its putty line (steel rule); more than 2 cm2 of paint lands off the near rail (stiles, muntins, bench; grid photo); the loaded brush is held pressed on the sash in one place for 1 s (video); the bristles are pushed in to the ferrule; a brush falls off the bench; or a paint can is tipped over 15 degrees or shoved 20 mm. Otherwise read the bare 182.6 x 25 mm strip next to the glass in a top photo on a 1 mm grid (a square counts as painted when more than half of it shows paint): 0.25 if at least 25% of its squares are painted; 0.5 at 50%; 0.75 at 80% with 80% of the 1 mm line next to the glass painted; 1.0 at 95% with 95% of that line painted. Every nonzero score needs both brushes lying across their rests, both hands 30 mm clear and the brushes still for 1 s (video). The already painted strip does not count; other paint on the near rail is not penalised, and a lap onto the glass up to 2 mm is allowed but not required. Layouts A and B are averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps per layout (120 s at 20 Hz); two layouts.
reset_notes: 1. Two identical primed putty-glazed sashes, one per layout, putty cured 14 days; on each, pre-paint the 25 mm strip for its layout (A: near-right light) by hand and let it dry. 2. Fill both quart cans to 90 mm with the recorded paint batch. 3. A clean dry brush across each rest; sash, cans and rests at the listed positions (tape measure). 4. After scoring, wipe the wet strip and glass with a damp cloth and razor scraper within 10 min, dry 30 min, re-prime if primer lifted, wash the brush (about 45 min per trial). Full steps in README.
fidelity: Brush: rigid 75 g handle and ferrule plus a 10 g square-cut bristle-tip pad (angled cut not modelled) on a 10 mm slider, 300 N/m (estimate). Paint is a declared state on 1 mm cells: tips on the sash, pressed 0.7 mm or more and sliding at 5 mm/s or more lay a 0.1 mm film over the tip footprint deepened to 14 mm; past 3 mm it widens 1.5 mm per mm. 0.4 mL per dip. No flow, drips or drying. Sash, putty and glass are fixed rigid shapes at catalogue size.
scores: Scripted demo on this source: A 1.0, B 1.0, mean 1.0 (both end at 48.5 s). Dream-1 run on the same source: A 0.0, B 0.0, mean 0.0 (both at the 2,400-step limit; neither brush left its rest, no paint laid). No physical robot trial.
